question.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5{x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}) \\  & =4\cdot 5{x}^{3}+2\cdot 4x \\  & =20{x}^{3}+8x\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(20{x}^{3}+8x) \\  & =3\cdot 20{x}^{2}+8 \\  & =60{x}^{2}+8.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\left(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}\right)+x-8\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\right)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\left(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}\right)+x-8\left(4{x}^{-1/2}\right)) \\  & =4\left(8\cdot \frac{{x}^{7}}{4}\right)+1-8\left((-\frac{1}{2})\cdot 4{x}^{-3/2}\right) \\  & =4\left(2{x}^{7}\right)+1+8\left(2{x}^{-3/2}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(4\left(2{x}^{7}\right)+1+8\left(2{x}^{-3/2}\right)) \\  & =4\left(7\cdot 2{x}^{6}\right)+0+8\left((-\frac{3}{2})\cdot 2{x}^{-5/2}\right) \\  & =4\left(14{x}^{6}\right)-8\left(3{x}^{-5/2}\right) \\  & =4\left(14{x}^{6}\right)-8\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\left(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}\right)+x-5\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{x}}\right)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\left(\frac{{x}^{8}}{4}\right)+x-5\left(4{x}^{-1/2}\right)) \\  & =6\left(8\cdot \frac{{x}^{7}}{4}\right)+1-5\left((-\frac{1}{2})\cdot 4{x}^{-3/2}\right) \\  & =6\left(2{x}^{7}\right)+1+5\left(2{x}^{-3/2}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(6\left(2{x}^{7}\right)+1+5\left(2{x}^{-3/2}\right)) \\  & =6\left(7\cdot 2{x}^{6}\right)+0+5\left((-\frac{3}{2})\cdot 2{x}^{-5/2}\right) \\  & =6\left(14{x}^{6}\right)-5\left(3{x}^{-5/2}\right) \\  & =6\left(14{x}^{6}\right)-5\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{{x}^{5}}}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x+6\left(\frac{1}{6{x}^{2}}\right)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\ln x+6\left(\frac{1}{6}{x}^{-2}\right)) \\  & =\frac{1}{x}+6\left(\frac{1}{6}\cdot (-2){x}^{-2-1}\right) \\  & ={x}^{-1}-6\left(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{-1}-6\left(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}\right)) \\  & =(-1){x}^{-1-1}-6\left(\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-3){x}^{-3-1}\right) \\  & =6\left(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\right)-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the first derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\left(\ln x\right)+4\left(\frac{1}{6{x}^{2}}\right)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\left(\ln x\right)+4\left(\frac{1}{6}{x}^{-2}\right)) \\  & =5\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+4\left(\frac{1}{6}\cdot (-2){x}^{-2-1}\right) \\  & =5\left({x}^{-1}\right)-4\left(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(5\left({x}^{-1}\right)-4\left(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}\right)) \\  & =5\left((-1){x}^{-1-1}\right)-4\left(\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-3){x}^{-3-1}\right) \\  & =4\left(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\right)-5\left(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7\left(\ln x\right)+3\left(\frac{1}{6{x}^{2}}\right)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7\left(\ln x\right)+3\left(\frac{1}{6}{x}^{-2}\right)) \\  & =7\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+3\left(\frac{1}{6}\cdot (-2){x}^{-2-1}\right) \\  & =7\left({x}^{-1}\right)-3\left(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the second derivative, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(7\left({x}^{-1}\right)-3\left(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{-3}\right)) \\  & =7\left((-1){x}^{-1-1}\right)-3\left(\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-3){x}^{-3-1}\right) \\  & =3\left(\frac{1}{{x}^{4}}\right)-7\left(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\right).\end{aligned}
$$
